subject: TLS rotation & DNS failover — private endpoint evacuation checklist
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@acme-corp.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Unable to reach private endpoint after cert rotation - urgent

Hi Rafael,

Over the last hour our staging services started failing TLS handshakes to the private endpoint your team manages (staging-api.acme.internal). We see clients refusing the server cert with an error that looks like a SAN mismatch, and some clients drop connections mid-request. Attached: screenshot_tls_error.png and our inventory of certificates mapped to DNS names (acme_cert_inventory.csv).

This is impacting QA and a handful of customer-sim tests. Can your team confirm whether a certificate rotation or DNS delegation change happened on Redwood's side? If so, we need an immediate mitigation path (DNS failover to the previous host or a quick cert rollback). We are available for a maintenance window starting 18:00 UTC today.

- Aaron (ops@acme-corp.com)
Ops Team, Acme Corp

---
Attachments: screenshot_tls_error.png (image/png), acme_cert_inventory.csv (text/csv)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unable to reach private endpoint after cert rotation - urgent

Aaron — thanks for the heads-up and for the artifacts. I'm pulling the on-call infra and TLS team in.

Quick clarifying Qs before we mobilize:
- Which FQDN(s) are failing (you mentioned staging-api.acme.internal — any aliases/service records?)
- Is this observed from a single region or from multiple client locations?

We can aim for the 18:00 UTC window. Neha, Marissa, Karthik — can you confirm the last rotation event for `staging-api.acme.internal` and whether Redwood pushed a new cert or a CA trust change in the last 6 hours? If we need to do an emergency failover, we should predefine roles and the rollback path now.

I'll coordinate comms with Acme. Rafael

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 16:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unable to reach private endpoint after cert rotation - urgent

On it — short checklist and immediate owners: 

1) Rapid assessment (owner: Neha) — take inventory (confirm cert chain, SANs, CA used).
   - Command: openssl s_client -connect staging-api.acme.internal:443 -servername staging-api.acme.internal
   - Verify: certificate SubjectAltName includes expected internal FQDNs; chain terminates in Redwood Private CA v2 (if we issued) or customer-managed CA.

2) DNS sanity (owner: Marissa) — confirm current A/AAAA records and recent updates; check TTLs and whether any split-horizon mapping changed.

3) Client trust mapping (owner: Karthik) — are clients pinning CA fingerprint or expecting an older intermediate? If so, prepare short-lived fallback using previous intermediate or instruct clients to accept the new root (only if safe).

4) Failover plan (owner: Rafael) — options:
   - Quick DNS rollback to previous address (if TTL allows immediate switch).
   - Route traffic via internal proxy that presents the old cert (if we have a cached PKI object and legal approval).
   - Emergency reissue of cert with requested SANs (if CA can issue within maintenance window).

5) Comms & approvals (owner: Rafael) — confirm maintenance window with Acme and Security.

I'll attach the internal playbook (cert-rotation-playbook.pdf) and a short script to dump cert SANs. We should treat this as a high-severity cert-ops incident and limit changes to the rollback options first.

Neha

---
Attachments: cert-rotation-playbook.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unable to reach private endpoint after cert rotation - urgent

I confirmed DNS from our authoritative private zone for Acme staging: zone `acme.internal` (split-horizon configured) — last change was a PTR/A update at 2026-09-02T09:12:13Z pushed by our provisioning pipeline (change id: prov-68421). That change updated a backend pool IP for `staging-api` but did NOT change CNAMEs.

Immediate notes:
- TTL for the A record is 60s in the internal view and 3600s in the public view. Since this is split-horizon, clients inside their VPC may still see the older IP if their DNS cache hasn't expired.
- If we need to fail back, I'll queue a direct edit to the internal zone to point staging-api to the previous host (rollback-ip: 10.12.5.42). We can do this now with an automated change that has an audit trail.

Commands to sanity-check that view (run from their VPC or via a bastion):
- dig @10.0.0.2 staging-api.acme.internal +short
- nslookup staging-api.acme.internal 10.0.0.2

I'll attach the mapping workbook (dns-failover-mapping.xlsx) showing the current and previous mappings.

Marissa

---
Attachments: dns-failover-mapping.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 18:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unable to reach private endpoint after cert rotation - urgent

Adding operational timeline and rollback sequence. Quoting Aditya's note below for context.

> On Wed, Sep 2, 2026 at 17:12, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> > We pushed the new intermediate (Redwood Private CA v2) at 09:00 UTC as part of the scheduled on-prem sync. Most hosts were validated, but I see staging-api was flagged as a non-standard SAN set and should have been excluded; looks like that exclusion didn't apply due to a templating bug.
>
Planned timeline (all times UTC):
- 18:00 — Maintenance window start (notify Acme and Security).
- 18:05 — Marissa performs DNS rollback to 10.12.5.42 for internal view (expected effect within ~60s for most clients).
- 18:10 — Neha validates cert chain on a sample of 3 client nodes and attempts openssl handshakes.
- 18:20 — Karthik performs traffic smoke tests and watches for 502/525s on the proxy layer.
- 18:30 — If clients are stable, mark incident mitigated and coordinate a root cause postmortem.
- 18:35 — If rollback fails, option B is emergency reissue; that requires CA approval and will take at least 10-20 minutes.

Rollback sequence (if DNS rollback not sufficient):
1) Apply upstream proxy rewrite to present previous cert (requires legal + security signoff).
2) Reissue cert with corrected SANs and push within emergency window.
3) As final resort, temporary client relaxation (not preferred) with explicit Security approval.

Karthik

---
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@acme-corp.com>, Security <security@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: Unable to reach private endpoint after cert rotation - urgent

Aaron — thanks for reporting this. We will execute the rollback plan in the 18:00 UTC window you proposed. Summary of agreed actions:
- 18:05 UTC: Marissa will perform internal DNS rollback to 10.12.5.42 (internal view).
- 18:10 UTC: Neha will confirm cert chain and SANs on sample clients.
- 18:20 UTC: Karthik will run smoke tests and confirm service health.
- Post-mitigation: Redwood will produce a postmortem and permanent fix for the templating exclusion that allowed the staging host to pick up the new intermediate.

Please standby for a follow-up at 18:30 UTC with results. Rafael
